comments.value: Same happens to me. I am on linux, but also having to run on a phone network tethered. Once it drops, it doesn't come back. But you are able to still talk with those still in the instance with you. But it isn't just social, but avatar changes too.

details:
1. Open VRChat

2. Organically or artificially interrupt your connection to VRChat

3. Under my context of Social/Friends being a separate server to the gameserver, note that there's no logfile entries listed under "Debug" concerning this supposedly separate server. No connections are logged as ever establishing, breaking, or reconnecting, only authorizations.

4. Observe that after this disconnection event, no social updates such as status, group broadcasts, or invites are received by the client. 

Included duplicate/co-evolved bug tickets that APPEAR to be referencing this issue:

[INTERESTED] https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/1137-friends-list-not-updating

https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/social-aspectsnotifications-breaking-upon-vrchat-connection-timeout

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/forced-status-updates-in-social

https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/vrchat-giving-fake-locations-of-friends

https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/my-vrchat-keeps-breaking

Thoughts:

There doesn't seem to be any attempt made by the client to recover the API session, connection, or to start a new API session or connection to this social server in the event that a disconnection happens.

There isn't really a clear recommendation for me, as letting the client submit a new connection on drop could lead to API request storms during outages that can worsen overloads or (excessively!) amplify throughput.

I have two plausible solutions to explore-- timing API sessions such that every hour(?) it forcefully creates a new session (but this will permanently increase API throughput and demand), or to create a new social API session on world change for the client so that simply clicking "rejoin" could resolve a dead social server connection for some. (This will also permanently increase API throughput and demand, but presumably less so since it'll go more towards the average time in world, hopefully over 1 hour, while also creating better troubleshooting possibilities.)

Neither of these options are graceful or good, but may stand to help the growing number of users that seem to be caught by this weird quirk. These thoughts come with a knowledge that any API solution is fragile and needs to be treated with care when making changes that result in additional requests. 

Additional context:

I'm a user that will always be unusually susceptible to this problem since I am on a custom "carrier-like" network that not only has a hardware firewall involved (that doesn't play nicely with vrchat at times, specifically this server), as well as hosted servers and services on the same WAN IP; and so I expect jank from my network.

That having been said, I'm noticing routine issues from within my friend circles that describe the same symptom as me, and I think it's time for me to at least make mention of/offer myself for testing or additional input on this issue. I'm a patient power user, my friends are not!

Current reliable workarounds:

Restarting VRChat

Large Settings > Switch Account > Yes > Log in using same credentials (Has the benefit of preserving tracking calibration/environment)

Contactable @ceraso on discord or at ceraso.42@gmail.com for additional input.

(Yes I monitor these, and I understand the consequences of posting these, they're public for a reason. I take abuse seriously ;) )
title: API: Client makes no attempt to reconnect to "Social and Friends" API on interruption
